text:
eli: Hey team — first day! I'm following the quickstart but my Rails app can't connect to Postgres in the compose stack. db container is running but app logs show:

eli: ```
ActiveRecord::ConnectionNotEstablished: PG::ConnectionBad: could not translate host name "db" to address: Name or service not known
```

maria: did you `docker-compose up` with the right project name? show `docker ps` and `docker network ls`.

eli: docker ps shows postgres and redis up. network shows project_default. I can `docker exec -it <postgres> psql -U postgres` and it works. app container can't resolve `db` though.

sam: Are you running the Rails dev server on the host or inside a container? In compose, service names resolve on the compose network only between containers.

eli: Running the dev server on my host (fast file reloads). I had DATABASE_URL pointing at `db` — so that explains it. How do I connect from the host to the DB in Docker?

maria: If your app runs on the host, use `localhost` and a mapped port. In your compose service for postgres do:
```yaml
ports:
  - "5432:5432"
```
then set DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@localhost:5432/dev
Or on Mac/Win you can use `host.docker.internal`. On Linux, use `extra_hosts` or `host-gateway`.

eli: ohh I had just `ports:
  - "5432"` (no host mapping) — that was the mistake. updating compose now.

eng-infra-bot: (deploy-bot) image postgres:15 pulled successfully :white_check_mark:

eli: fixed! app connects now. Also redis was failing because I had REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379 which obviously pointed to my host instead of the container — switched to localhost with port mapping and it's fine.

sam: Pro tip: we have a `dev-ports` compose profile that exposes common ports and adds `extra_hosts` for host.docker.internal mounting. Ping @devex if you want it in your dotfiles.

maria: Also note Docker Desktop on mac sometimes binds 5432 on the host already — if you hit weird errors run `lsof -i:5432` and kill any local Postgres. Welcome aboard, Eli! :wave:

eli: Thanks everyone, super helpful. Saving this convo for future new-hires. :tada:
